channel.title: BioFarmLab — Knowledge
channel.description: Knowledge about soil biology, compost and regenerative agriculture.

item.title: Homemade fertilizers: what are you actually giving the plant?
item.description: What banana-peel water provides, how compost supports the soil food web, and why plant ferments, compost extract and compost tea are different preparations.

item.title: Bought soil hardened into clods after rain. Where should I start?
item.description: Why bought soil can form hard clods after rain, how compaction differs from surface crusting, and how soil organisms help build a porous structure.

item.title: I added EM, but my compost still is not heating up. What am I missing?
item.description: Why adding a microbial product does not ensure hot compost: the roles of microbial activity, moisture, air, materials and heat retention.

item.title: Compost Calculator: plan a pile with the materials you have
item.description: Calculate compost pile volume, ingredient proportions and an estimated carbon-to-nitrogen ratio (C:N) with BioFarmLab’s Living Soil Shortcut app.

item.title: Compost Log: keep the history of your compost pile
item.description: Keep temperature, moisture and process history together with Compost Log, part of BioFarmLab’s Living Soil Shortcut app and course package.

item.title: Soil Radar: record your soil observations and compare seasons
item.description: See the actual Soil Radar in BioFarmLab’s Living Soil Shortcut app: saved plots, a five-axis chart and observations you can revisit over time.

item.title: When is compost ready to use?
item.description: How to recognise mature compost: stable temperature, earthy smell, crumbly texture and an assessment of its biology under the microscope.

item.title: Soil Food Web for beginners: a practical course and app
item.description: Start learning soil food web biology with Living Soil Shortcut: 28 practical lessons plus Soil Radar, Compost Calculator and Compost Log. Compare beginner learning options.

item.title: Chemical vs. biological soil testing: what does each one tell you?
item.description: Chemical testing measures pH and selected nutrients. Microscopy-based biological assessment shows the presence and proportions of major organism groups. The two methods answer different questions.

item.title: Can fertilizer replace soil biology?
item.description: Fertilizer can supply nutrients, but it does not replace decomposition, nutrient cycling, root–microbe interactions or the biological contribution to soil structure.

item.title: Choosing a compost turner for your tractor: BioFarmLab 10 and 40 kW
item.description: Got a tractor? Compare BioFarmLab compost turners, PTO drive, windrow size, watering, current prices and delivery. Clear answers to common buyer questions.

item.title: Soil or compost problem? Find the cause before you add another product
item.description: Field observation, chemistry, biological assessment and compost process signals provide different information. Start with the question you need answered.

item.title: Why is my compost pile not heating up?
item.description: A compost pile stays cool when microbial activity is limited or when the heat being produced escapes too quickly. The same symptom can have several causes.
